sources.entry: Dolphin - Powerful emulator for Nintendo GameCube and Wii games.

summary.one_liner: Dolphin is a GPLv2+ emulator for running GameCube and Wii games on Windows, Linux, macOS, and recent Android devices.
summary.what_it_does: Dolphin emulates GameCube and Wii games on desktop (Windows, Linux, macOS) and Android. The README documents a command-line interface for launching files, NAND titles, or movies, setting config options, loading save states, running without a UI in batch mode, and choosing video backends (D3D, D3D12, OGL, Vulkan, Null, Software Renderer) and audio emulation (HLE or LLE). It also describes DolphinTool, a companion CLI with commands to convert disc images to RVZ, ISO, GCZ or WIA formats, verify images with checksums, print image headers, and extract partitions and files from disc images. The README links to build instructions on the project wiki and includes Gradle/CMake notes for building the Android app.
use_cases: Play GameCube games on a computer
Play Wii games on a computer or Android device
Convert disc images to RVZ or ISO
Extract files from GameCube or Wii disc images
Run games headless from the command line
how_to_run: Build following the platform-specific wiki instructions (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android)
Android: import the Gradle project in ./Source/Android into Android Studio
notable: Supports both GameCube and Wii games across desktop and Android
DolphinTool CLI for converting, verifying, and extracting disc images
Multiple graphics backends including Direct3D, OpenGL, and Vulkan
Selectable DSP emulation: fast HLE or accurate LLE
caveats: Requires a CPU with SSE2 and a reasonably modern GPU (Direct3D 11.1 / OpenGL 3.3 minimum)
Windows 10 1903+ and macOS 11.0+ required; other Unix-like systems are unsupported
Android needs Android 7.0+ and 64-bit ARMv8 or x86-64; performance varies with GPU driver quality
Building from source requires submodules and platform-specific setup described on the wiki
